extracted.intended_audience: museum staff who applied for or received IMLS Museums for America (MFA) grants; grantees and applicants participating in program evaluation interviews/surveys
extracted.subtask_description: A structured survey instrument and interview protocol used to collect standardized information from MFA applicants and grantees about (a) unfunded application experience, (b) awarded project characteristics and activities, (c) partners and audiences, and (d) short- and long-term effects and sustainability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Redesign and resubmission of previous unfunded MFA project
rubrics_metrics.description: Is this application the redesign and resubmission of a previous unfunded IMLS-MFA project?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Response options: Yes / No / Don't know. Used to identify whether current unfunded application is a revision of a prior MFA submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resubmission of unfunded MFA project to different IMLS program
rubrics_metrics.description: Did your museum resubmit this MFA unfunded project to a different IMLS grant program?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Response options: Yes / No / Don't know. If yes, follow-up asks whether the museum received IMLS funding from the non-MFA grant program for this application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission of unfunded MFA project to non-IMLS funder
rubrics_metrics.description: Did your museum submit this MFA unfunded project to a non-IMLS funder?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Response options: Yes / No / Don't know. If yes, follow-up asks whether funding was received from the non-IMLS funder.

rubrics_metrics.name: Execution of any version of unfunded project
rubrics_metrics.description: Were you able to execute any version of this MFA unfunded project?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Response options: Yes / No / Don't know. Captures whether organizations proceeded with implementation despite not receiving MFA funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Perceptions of fairness and usefulness regarding unfunded application
rubrics_metrics.description: Extent of agreement with statements about the unfunded application: (a) We believe our application was given full and fair consideration; (b) The reviewer's comments were useful for redesigning the project; (c) IMLS staff was helpful in providing feedback.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Response scale: Strongly disagree / Disagree / Agree / Strongly agree / Don't know/Not applicable. Includes open-ended question: 'What other aspects of the unfunded application should IMLS know about?'

rubrics_metrics.name: Type of awarded project
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicate the type of award project: ongoing continuation of prior awarded project; new project likely/did lead to continuation (not an extension); new project which will not/did not lead to continuation (not an extension).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to categorize award lifecycle and continuity planning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respondent's level of knowledge about awarded project
rubrics_metrics.description: Please indicate your level of knowledge about this awarded project: Very knowledgeable / Somewhat knowledgeable / No one affiliated is knowledgeable about this project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determines reliability of responses and whether to reassign survey to another staff member.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of partner organizations involved
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify types of partner organizations that expended cash or in-kind resources on the project, including museum/library partners (e.g., aquarium, art museum, history museum, library, specialized museum, zoo, etc.), government organizations (state, local/county, city), non-government/community organizations (health facilities, family services, youth organizations, senior services, arts organizations, legal services, media, civic organizations, businesses, other nonprofits), education partners (elementary, secondary, 4-year colleges, community colleges), and other partners (policy/research organizations, other).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check all that apply; in-kind defined as goods/services rather than cash; include 'No partner' if none in category; space for 'Other; please specify.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Planned project activity categories
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicate whether the MFA project included the following activity types in the proposal: Programming; Exhibitions; Digitization; Collections; Technology and Online Resources; Organizational Development (training, hiring, contracting, research/evaluation/survey programs, management plans, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Response per category: Yes / No. Provides high-level activity taxonomy for evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extent of programming activities planned
rubrics_metrics.description: For specified programming activities (concerts, film festivals, live performances, broadcasts, demonstrations/workshops, lectures, community discussion groups, education programs at institution, in-school programs, afterschool programs, curriculum guides, interpretive programs/materials, classes/institutes, training sessions, conferences, internships/mentoring/apprenticeships, other), indicate extent of activity planned: Not included in this project / Develop new programs or materials / Enhance existing programs or materials / Continue existing programs or materials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Captures whether proposal intended development, enhancement, continuation, or omission of each program type; includes free-text for 'other'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Status of planned programming activities
rubrics_metrics.description: For each planned programming activity, indicate status: Will not or did not conduct as planned / Still in progress during grant period / Completed during grant period / Don't know.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Asked separately for each programming subtype (concerts, film festivals, etc.) to track implementation status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of exhibits planned and status
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicate if the project planned the following exhibit types and their status: upgrade/expand current exhibit (e.g., accessibility such as multi-languages, Braille), develop concept for new exhibit, research new exhibit, plan new exhibit, fabricate a new exhibit, create traveling exhibit, other.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Status options: Exhibit was not planned / Exhibit was planned but will not/did not do / Still in progress during grant period / Completed during grant period / Don't know. Space for 'other' description.

rubrics_metrics.name: Digitization activities and status
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicate whether the project planned digitization activities and their status: digitize collections; convert non-digital content to digital; repurpose digital content (e.g., for educational purposes); create new digital content; other.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Status options: Was not planned / Planned but will not/did not do / Still in progress / Completed / Don't know. Also asks what portion of collections would be covered (None, <10%, 10–25%, 25–50%, 50–75%, >75% but <100%, 100%, Not sure).

rubrics_metrics.name: Collections activities and status
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicate planned collections activities and status: inventory collections; move collections; create public collections finding guides; create new collections management guidelines/procedures; implement new collections management system; other.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Status options same as other activity sections. Includes space to describe 'other'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technology and online resources activities and status
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicate planned technology activities and status: update or create new website; create online access to collections records or information; purchase technology equipment; consolidate multiple databases; develop searchable online database; upgrade/purchase/install new software; create audio tour; create online exhibition; develop high-tech interactive exhibition; other.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Status options as above. Space for 'other' description.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organizational development activities and status
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicate planned organizational activities and status: provide staff/volunteer/docent training (including technology); hire full-time staff; hire part-time staff; hire a consultant; contract for services (fabrication, design, security); train interpreters/volunteers/docents; create or expand interpreter/docent/volunteer program; support research and evaluation program (including conducting surveys); develop key management plans (comprehensive interpretive plan, emergency plans, collections management plans); other.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Status options as above. Includes space for 'other' description.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other planned activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicate if there were any other activities not covered in previous questions; for each planned activity enter description and indicate status (Will not do as planned / Still in progress / Completed).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides catch-all for activities outside predefined categories; allows listing multiple items.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unplanned project activities
rubrics_metrics.description: List any activities that were not planned in the proposal but are in progress or completed, with status (Still in progress / Completed).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Captures emergent or opportunistic activities resulting from the grant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audience groups directly served
rubrics_metrics.description: Which groups were/are directly served by this project? (select all that apply): paid staff; unpaid staff (docents, interns, volunteers); adult learners; seniors; parents; youth; students; administrators; professionals; residents of particular neighborhood/community; policymakers; persons with disabilities; low income citizens; specific racial/ethnic communities; families; not group-specific; other (specify).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes prompts for brief descriptions where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Age groups served
rubrics_metrics.description: Age groups served by your grant project (select all that apply): preschool; grades K-5; grades 6-8; grades 9-12; post high school/young adults (18-25); adults (26-64); seniors (65+); multi-age/family; other (specify).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to profile target audience by age segments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Main area of resource investment
rubrics_metrics.description: Taking into account resources (money, staffing) spent/being spent on this project, in which area was most of the project resources invested? Select one: Programming / Exhibits / Digitization / Collections / Technology and online resources / Organizational development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identifies primary focus of resource allocation for cost-effectiveness or priority analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Short-term organizational effects (programming)
rubrics_metrics.description: Select organizational effects or changes shortly after project completion related to programming: grant-funded programming continued beyond grant; sustained grant-funded programming; did not sustain grant-funded programming; sought additional funding to sustain programming; developed related programming to expand value of grant-funded program; expanded range of possibilities for programs or exhibitions; other; no changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multiple selection allowed; includes 'other' text field.

rubrics_metrics.name: Short-term organizational capacity effects
rubrics_metrics.description: Select organizational capacity changes resulting from the project: enhanced staff capacity in program development; enhanced staff capacity in creating new kinds of exhibitions; enhanced staff capacity in reaching new or larger audiences; enhanced staff capacity in forming external partnerships; enhanced staff capacity in working internally across departments; enhanced staff capacity in using outcomes-based evaluation; improved staff cohesion and commitment to mission; greater alignment of staff responsibilities with mission; greater board involvement; helped institution fulfill its mission (e.g., meet benchmarks); increased ability to attract outside funding; decreased ability to attract outside funding; other; no effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multiple selection allowed; captures both positive and negative capacity outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Short-term audience effects
rubrics_metrics.description: Select short-term audience effects: reached new audiences (e.g., youth, families, minorities); increased commitment by existing audiences; changes in regular audience participation; increased audience access (expanded hours, mobile programming); other; no effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to measure immediate audience reach and access improvements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Short-term community profile effects
rubrics_metrics.description: Select community profile effects: changed institutional identity; strengthened museum’s public image; raised institution’s prestige in its community; increased local media coverage; increased visibility as a center of community learning; other; no change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assesses reputation and public positioning changes attributable to the grant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Short-term partnerships effects
rubrics_metrics.description: Select effects on building partnerships: improved skills in building partnerships; strengthened ongoing partnerships; developed new partnerships; partnerships with schools or Institutes of Higher Education; with youth organizations; with other museums/historical societies; with other community organizations; developed new types of partnerships; decreased ability to attract partners; increased ability to attract more partners; other; no effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Captures both qualitative and structural partnership outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effects due to partnerships
rubrics_metrics.description: Select effects that resulted from partnerships: brought in new audiences; brought in new resources not normally available to organization; brought in new staff, paid or unpaid; brought in new memberships; raised community awareness of organization; other; no effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identifies tangible contributions partnerships produced for the organization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open-ended short-term effects
rubrics_metrics.description: If there are any other short-term effects not covered above, please describe (free-text).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Captures additional impacts not anticipated by checklist items.

rubrics_metrics.name: Success continuing new programming
rubrics_metrics.description: If the grant project enabled new programming, to what extent has your organization been successful in continuing the programs? Options: Not at all successful / Somewhat successful / Very successful / No new programming.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow-up asks for reasons attributed to not continuing programs (free-text).

rubrics_metrics.name: Success sustaining new audiences
rubrics_metrics.description: If the grant enabled you to bring in new audiences, to what extent has your organization been successful in sustaining these new audiences? Options: Not at all successful / Somewhat successful / Very successful / No new audiences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow-up asks for reasons attributed to not sustaining new audiences (free-text).

rubrics_metrics.name: Relative grant size and sufficiency
rubrics_metrics.description: Was this MFA grant from IMLS larger, smaller, or about the same as other grants you may have received? Options: Larger / Smaller / About the same / No other grant(s) received. Were the MFA grant funds sufficient to complete the planned project activities? Options: No / Somewhat / Yes / Don't know.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assesses comparability and adequacy of funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Long-term effects on organization
rubrics_metrics.description: Please describe any long-term effect(s) that the MFA project has had on your organization (free-text).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Open prompt to capture sustained organizational changes attributable to the grant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Long-term effects on community and relationships
rubrics_metrics.description: Please describe any long-term effect(s) that the MFA project has had on your community or community relationships (free-text).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Open prompt to capture enduring community-level impacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unexpected long-term effects
rubrics_metrics.description: Please describe any UNEXPECTED long-term effect(s) that the MFA project has had on your organization, community or community relationships (free-text).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Captures unintended or emergent consequences of the project over time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best Practices interview: project background
rubrics_metrics.description: Interview prompts to capture project history and rationale: Could you share the history of this project? How did the idea originate? What audience/community issue or need was the project designed to address? How does this project align with your institution’s mission?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Semi-structured qualitative protocol to produce a short Best Practices Profile; interview ~1 hour.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best Practices interview: implementation and sustainability
rubrics_metrics.description: Interview prompts about implementation and sustainability: Which aspects of the project were most successful and what key factors drove success? What challenges were encountered and how were they met? What does sustainability mean for this project and how have components been supported since grant period? What are key learnings/advice for others?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Open-ended probes to surface implementation lessons and sustainability strategies for replication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best Practices interview: partnerships
rubrics_metrics.description: Interview prompts about partnerships: Did the project involve partnering with other organizations? With whom were key partnerships formed? What was the value of partnerships to your institution and to partners? Have partnerships been maintained and if so how? What has grown out of them?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explores partnership formation, value-add, longevity, and downstream effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best Practices interview: community effects and reputation
rubrics_metrics.description: Interview prompts about community effects: How did target/existing audiences respond to the program? What trends were observed over time? How has target audience involvement continued or grown? How has the project changed your museum’s reputation or position in the community and what indications of reputation change have you observed?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Qualitative probes to assess audience reception and reputation outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Survey completion and follow-up contact consent
rubrics_metrics.description: Survey completion page asks how many people were involved in filling out the survey and offers to send the Museums for America Grant Survey Executive Summary; asks whether the museum's name may be included in the final report and requests contact information (name, title, organization, address, email).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Captures respondent consent for attribution and provides proxy for follow-up or dissemination of results.
